synth.summary:
The 14 claimed values can be trusted as computed. The caveats concern how the row compares with other rows, not the values themselves.

- **Values reproduce.** I recomputed them from the stored metrics_summary.json files myself: the largest difference is 0.0005, every checkpoint.txt says epoch_24.pth, and latest.pth points to epoch_24.pth. The verifiers also reproduced them from the raw results_nusc.json through the PCCR evaluation path (94 fields per rig, difference 0) and with two separately written from-scratch evaluators (identical per-class APs on all 14 rigs).
- **Right data per rig.** Each rig's results contain exactly its own 1800 test tokens. A CPU re-run of epoch_24 on each rig's own images matched the stored boxes (within 8.2 cm and 0.0032 score). Feeding R1's images instead puts the boxes 11 to 19 m off.
- **Clean training.** Training used R1 train only, and the test towns (Town03/06/07) never appear in it. The final epoch was used, with no epoch picked on test. Test inputs carry no ground truth (GT).
- **No sign of leakage.** The predictions look like a real detector's. R1 val (41.67) is higher than R1 test (34.54), the opposite of what test leakage would do.
- **Frame chain is correct.** Feeding GT in as predictions gives mAP 100 on R1, R4, R5, R6, R9 and R1-f.
- No lens found an issue above low severity, so no skeptic refutations were run.

**Caveats (comparisons only):**
- BEVFormer keeps all 300 boxes per sample with no score floor. BEVDepth has a 0.1 floor, and applying it to BEVFormer costs 1.3 points on R1.
- On R4, R5, R6, R8 and R9 the vehicle-fixed frame differs from the LiDAR frame that the PETR† and Fast-BEV† rows used. The size of this effect has not been measured.
- There is only one training run, so seed-to-seed noise is unknown.
- Only 15 of the 25,200 test samples were re-run.

**The older row is not reproduced.** Ours is higher by 13.4 (R1), 13.2 (R1-c6) and 8.0 (R1-c10). The older row's code and settings are unknown, so the gap cannot be attributed to anything. The frame is ruled out for these three rigs. You need to supply the older row's code or settings before deciding which BEVFormer-S row goes in the table.

For context (docs/results.md): the older row's R1 of 21.1 is below BEVDet† 25.2, BEVFusion-C† 26.0 and our BEVDepth 30.43. Our 34.536 is below the BEVDepth [42] row in your table (36.85).
confirmed_problems: Score floor differs between the compared rows. BEVFormer keeps all 300 boxes per sample (max_num=300; the config sets no score_threshold), while BEVDepth's results contain no box below 0.1. Applying a 0.1 floor to BEVFormer gives R1 33.228 (-1.31), R5 8.097 (-0.43) and R9 12.258 (-0.74). Impact: this accounts for 0.4 to 1.3 points of the BEVFormer-vs-BEVDepth gap. R1 still favours BEVFormer (33.2 vs 30.4), and the claimed values are unaffected.

The frame differs from the dagger rows' frame on five rigs. BEVFormer uses the vehicle-fixed frame (ref2ego [-0.46,0,1.86]); PETR† and Fast-BEV† used each rig's own LiDAR frame. On the 9 etron rigs the two frames are identical. They differ on R4/R5/R8 (rig LiDAR sits at [+0.24,0,-0.36] in the ref frame), R6 ([+0.10,0,+2.94]) and R9 ([+3.06,0,+2.32]). Impact: on those 5 rigs, comparisons with the dagger rows (and with the older row, if it used the LiDAR frame) are not like-for-like, and the size of the effect is unmeasured. BEVDepth uses the ego frame and is consistent with BEVFormer. The table must state the frame.

The official zero-points filter keeps a different GT set on each rig. This is a property of the PCCR protocol, not an error in the claim. num_lidar_pts differs between same-vehicle rigs (30725 of 46369 matched objects). After filtering, adult GT is 4778 in R1 vs 1982 in R1-c10, and child GT is 1153 vs 380. Impact: without the filter the values drop by about 1.5 to 1.8 (R1 32.83), and the gaps between each rig and R1 move by at most 0.68. It applies the same way to every row.

Auditability gap. The test log does not echo the effective data_root or ann_file. A wrong data_root would silently load another rig's images, because the file names are the same in every rig and R1-f/r/t use R1's camera names. Only the KeyError raised by the evaluation's GT-table lookup guards against this. Impact: none here, since token matches and re-inference confirm each rig's own data. It is a latent risk for future runs, for example with format_only.

Orientation error is high (mAOE 1.02 to 1.27). This is genuine model error, not a convention bug: feeding GT through as predictions gives AOE of at most 0.0055. Impact: NDS and AOE only, not mAP. Side findings that affect no mAP: BEVDepth's adult AOE is 1.73 (above pi/2) with a flat |dyaw| histogram, and BEVDepth stores z as the box bottom.
refuted_problems: No skeptic refutation rounds ran because every lens issue was low severity. The concerns below were tested directly and ruled out.

Wrong rig data or a data_root mix-up: ruled out. Each results file holds exactly its rig's 1800 test tokens (0 missing, 0 extra), and no two rigs share any sample token. CPU re-inference of epoch_24 on 15 samples, using each rig's own images, reproduces the stored boxes within 8.2 cm and 0.0032 score. Wrong-image controls are 11.6 to 19.1 m off.

Stale files or transcription errors: ruled out. All 14 values match the metrics_summary.json files (my own check: largest difference 0.0005). Re-evaluating each results_nusc.json reproduces all 94 numeric fields with difference 0. Output timestamps run strictly in rig order, all after epoch_24.pth.

Wrong checkpoint, or an epoch chosen on test data: ruled out. All 14 rigs used epoch_24, the last epoch. An epoch_23 control deviates 10 to 100 times more than epoch_24. The per-epoch evaluation used R1 val (1020 samples), not test.

Metric errors (wrong classes, label permutation, tie handling): ruled out. Two from-scratch evaluators reproduce every per-class, per-threshold AP exactly on all 14 rigs. Only the 7 classes are present. Per-class median box sizes match the GT. Reversing the order of tied scores changes R1 by 0.0002.

GT leakage at test time: ruled out. Test inputs are only img and img_metas, with can_bus all zeros and no ann_info. There is no spike of predictions at zero distance from GT, and 0 predictions fall within 1 cm in centre and 1 mm in size. On R1, localisation quality is close to BEVDepth's (median 0.86 m vs 0.92 m). Val 41.67 is higher than test 34.54.
Train/test overlap: ruled out. Train, val and test share 0 scenes, 0 tokens and 0 image names. The test towns (Town03/06/07) do not appear in train.

Frame or conversion bug, including on other vehicles: ruled out. Feeding GT through as predictions gives mAP 100 with ATE and ASE 0 on R1, R4, R5, R6, R9 and R1-f. Projections match the devkit to 0.000 px on every camera. Predicted car bottoms on R6 and R9 sit at the GT height (-1.851 and -1.840 vs about -1.858).

Modified evaluation code or config drift: ruled out. check_pccr_eval_copy passes, and git is clean. The work-dir config differs from the repo config only in gpu_ids and work_dir, and the config embedded in the checkpoint is identical to the work-dir copy.

The BEVFormer-vs-BEVDepth gap being an evaluation artifact: ruled out. The same independent evaluator reproduces both rows, and the devkit eval code is identical in the two environments. Only the score-floor difference (at most 1.3 points) remains.
unchecked: Full re-inference was not done. Only 15 of the 25,200 test samples were re-run, on CPU. The rest rests on file-level evidence: one process per rig, exact token equality and exact re-evaluation.
Run-to-run variance. There is one training run, so the noise from training seeds behind the 3-decimal values is unknown.
How much the vehicle-fixed frame changes R4/R5/R6/R8/R9 compared with each rig's own LiDAR frame. Measuring it needs GPU inference with ref2ego=None.

How the older row (R1 21.1, R1-c6 19.6, R1-c10 26.2) was produced. Its code, training classes (7 or 9), metric definition, input resolution, initialisation, temporal setting, number of epochs, score floor, frame and GT filter are all unknown. Its R6 and R9 values, which would show its frame according to docs/decisions.md, are not in the claim. Its R1 value equals PETR†'s R1 (21.1), but its R1-c6 and R1-c10 do not match PETR†'s (18.8 and 21.0).
Whether the vendored third_party/pccr evaluation code equals upstream PCCR at commit 6798206, and whether tools/pccr_sha256.txt matches PCCR's official hashes.
Why num_lidar_pts differs between same-vehicle rigs in the PCCR tables.

Coverage limits. The prediction-vs-GT distance analysis covered only R1, R5, R9, R1-f and R2. The GT-as-prediction and box checks were not run on R1-c6, R1-c10, R1-r, R1-t, R2, R3, R5, R7 or R8. All 14 rigs were, however, reproduced by the independent evaluators.

Why BEVFormer stays robust across rigs (R1-f 24.7 vs BEVDepth 0.2; R2 23.4 vs 0.1). Only its reality was shown: on R1-f, median distance to GT is 1.07 m and 2 m GT coverage is 0.426, from R1-f's own images and intrinsics.
setup_facts_explaining_gap: Ruled out on the rigs the older row reports: the vehicle-fixed frame is exactly the LIDAR_TOP frame on etron rigs (R1, R1-c6, R1-c10, R1-f, R1-r, R1-t, R2, R3, R7). The frame choice therefore cannot cause the gaps of +13.4 (R1), +13.2 (R1-c6) and +8.0 (R1-c10).
Also ruled out: test leakage, choosing an epoch on test data, wrong rig data and evaluation artifacts (see the refuted list).
The gap is not uniform: +13.4, +13.2 and +8.0. The older row has R1-c10 above R1 by 5.1, while ours has R1-c10 below R1 by 0.3.

Training classes: we train only the 7 evaluated classes (num_classes 7; traffic_sign and traffic_light are removed by ObjectNameFilter). PCCR's dagger baselines trained on 9 classes. What the older row used is unknown.

Input: native 1280x720 at scale 1.0 (R1 test tensor 8x3x736x1280), with an R101 backbone that has DCNv2 in stages 3 and 4. The measured R1 gain over BEVDepth (384x704 input) is in the small classes: bicycle 49.9 vs 38.7, adult 39.1 vs 27.5, child 9.8 vs 2.4. Car and bus are lower (40.2/24.2 vs 43.0/27.9). The older row's resolution is unknown.

No score floor: all 300 boxes per sample are kept. A 0.1 floor would lower R1 by 1.31. This can explain at most about 1.3 of the 13.4-point R1 gap, and only if the older row used such a floor (unknown).

Evaluation: PCCR's evaluation code, copied verbatim, with the devkit filter that drops GT boxes with zero points. Without that filter, R1, R1-c6 and R1-c10 score 32.83, 31.03 and 32.78 (-1.7, -1.8 and -1.4). This can explain at most about 1.8 points, and only if the older row was evaluated differently (unknown).

Training recipe: 24 epochs over all 3780 R1-train samples. Batch 8 (2 GPUs x 1 sample x 4 accumulation steps). AdamW lr 2e-4 with backbone lr x0.1 and weight decay 0.01. Cosine schedule with a 2000-iteration linear warmup, i.e. 500 optimizer steps. Grad clip 35, GridMask and photometric distortion. The final epoch is used. R1 val was 36.64 at epoch 12 and plateaued at 40.5 to 41.7 over epochs 19 to 24. The older row's recipe is unknown.

Relative to upstream bevformer_small, our setup removes rather than adds components: single frame (queue_length 1, video_test_mode False), CAN bus off, ImageNet initialisation instead of the nuScenes-trained FCOS3D weights (load_from None), no velocity head (code_size 8) and cams_embeds off. None of these is shown to raise mAP, and their direction relative to the older row is unknown.

result.notes:
Verdict: no provenance problem found. Every claimed number traces back through four links, each checked with numbers above:
- **Metric files:** the 14 numbers equal the metrics_summary.json values to 3 decimals.
- **Results files:** each summary reproduces exactly from its results_nusc.json and that rig's own GT tables (94 numeric fields, max diff 0).
- **Inputs:** each results file contains exactly that rig's 1800 test tokens, and the sampled predictions reproduce from epoch_24 plus that rig's own images and calibration. Feeding R1's images instead gives errors of 11 to 19 m.
- **Training:** R1 train only, with disjoint val, test, scenes and towns; the config is the repo config; the single epoch-24 checkpoint was used for all rigs, and the test outputs were written strictly in rig order after it.

The high R1-f, R2 and R5 values against BEVDepth are therefore not caused by wrong data, wrong split, wrong checkpoint or stale files.

result.notes:
I found no evidence of GT leakage or implausible predictions. The predictions look like those of a genuine camera-only detector, and on R1 their localisation quality is close to vanilla BEVDepth's (median distance to nearest GT 0.86 m vs 0.92 m; 2 m GT coverage 0.565 vs 0.566). BEVFormer's higher mAP comes from small classes and higher precision, not from near-perfect boxes.

My first script (verify_bf/analyze_rig.py) printed 'recomputed mAP7 0.000' for every rig. That was a bug in my script, not in the repo: NuScenes DetectionMetrics.serialize() returns a defaultdict with float keys, so lookups with '0.5' returned 0. The corrected evaluation (verify_bf/gtleak/eval_only.py, which JSON round-trips the metrics) reproduces the stored files exactly. The distance statistics in analyze_rig.py do not use that dict and are unaffected.

issues.title: Comparability caveat, not a correctness defect: the BEVFormer-S row uses a vehicle-fixed frame, while the PCCR baseline rows that sampled heights in each rig's own LiDAR frame did not
issues.evidence: For the five non-etron rigs, the rig's own LIDAR_TOP frame sits at these offsets in the ref frame: [+0.24,0,-0.36] for R4/R5/R8, [+0.10,0,+2.94] for R6 and [+3.06,0,+2.32] for R9 (lidar2ego minus ref2ego). The ground therefore stays at -1.86 instead of -4.80 (R6) or -4.18 (R9). docs/decisions.md (2026-11-22) records this choice on purpose: PETR and Fast-BEV in PCCR (LiDAR frame) scored 0.0 on R6/R9. On the etron rigs (R1, R1-c6/c10/f/r/t, R2, R3, R7) the ref frame equals LIDAR_TOP exactly, so it has no effect there. Our vanilla BEVDepth row is also anchored to the vehicle: its car predictions sit at the same ego height on R1/R4/R6/R9 (bottom about -0.79 m on every rig), so BEVFormer vs BEVDepth is frame-consistent. Only the dagger rows are not.

result.notes: Under this lens the BEVFormer-S numbers hold. The vehicle-fixed frame is applied the same way in the train, val and test configs and survives the launcher's per-rig override. Every vehicle puts its ground at z = -1.86 in the ref frame (car bottom median -1.857 on R6 and -1.858 on R9). Cameras project exactly like the devkit, with a 0.000 px center difference on every R6, R9 and R1-f camera. The output chain ref -> ego -> global reproduces devkit boxes to about 4e-6 m, z included, with the same counts (31424/31424 on R6). The stored predictions on R6 and R9 sit at the right height (car bottom -1.851 and -1.840 vs GT -1.858 and -1.857). An evaluator written independently of PCCREvalMixin reproduces all 14 claimed mAPs exactly from the stored results_nusc.json files. Dataset structure worth knowing: the 14 rigs' test splits replay the same 30 Town03/06/07 scenes with identical ego poses, while sample tokens are unique per rig.
